title: Choose the visual world for اقعد فين؟
question: The roll assigned the Mashrabiya Shade world. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Your notes so far are built in: less text, the picture carries the answer, the 3D is on the result but loads after the numbers, phone and tablet.

options.label: ضل المشربية · Mashrabiya Shade
options.lineage: Cairo mashrabiya: the turned-wood lattice that cuts hard sun into cool shade and small, exact patches of light
options.thesis: Every result is the view from behind a mashrabiya: cool deep shade as the ground of the picture, and sunlight only where it really lands on your seats, cut into the patches the engine computed. It refuses the weather-app sky gradient, the sun icon on a glass card, and the notebook.
materials: turned-wood lattice that IS the seat grid
options.viewport: Form: a lime-plaster page, from and to as two stacked slabs with a swap, the day as an hour strip where lit cells show the sun's height, the vehicle as two silhouettes, and one full-width deep-shade button in the thumb zone. Result: the verdict in heavy Fatimid Kufi (Reem Kufi, 44 px) in shade teal, one short line under it, then the shade window: the microbus plan seen through the lattice, every seat a lattice cell, sun patches glowing amber exactly where computed, best seats ringed, and a label that always says الرحلة كلها or the exact minute. The real 3D microbus fades into the same window after the answer is already on screen.
options.risk: Mashrabiya can slide into tourist ornament; the lattice must stay functional (it is the seat grid and the trip strip), never wallpaper. A deep-shade window in noon glare needs very bright patches and big numbers.

raised.raise: Numbers are data: minutes and times in tabular columns at one weight, and the verdict holds a strict two-value contrast with nothing gray in between.
Every region is labeled by its literal name (الرحلة كلها, دلوقتي, ناحية السواق, ناحية الباب); wayfinding is reading, no decorative headings.
The verdict line never shrinks at any width; everything else gives way first.
One field dominates each screen (the shade window on the result); only the legend stays quiet and level.
The microbus and its seats appear as the real objects (the 3D model and a true plan), never as icons.

options.label: لافتة المترو · Metro Wayfinding
options.lineage: Cairo Metro and Egyptian railway station signage, departure boards (the Flighty model)
options.thesis: The answer as a platform sign: a bilingual direction sign with an arrow to your side, seats as a numbered board, the trip as a departure line with the sun's stretches marked.
options.viewport: A white sign panel: the verdict as a big direction sign with an arrow pointing to the good side of the drawn microbus, the seat board beside it, the trip as one departure row with sun bands.
options.risk: Also where most transit apps land: clear and effective, but familiar and less memorable.

options.label: لوحة الـ LED · Seven-Segment Board
options.lineage: terminal LED boards, the microbus dashboard clock, stadium scoreboards
options.thesis: Minutes and times as lit segments, shade as designed ghost cells, every seat a fixed cell in one rigid mask.
options.viewport: A matte black board: the sunny minutes per side as big segment numbers, seats as a mask of cells lit amber where the sun lands.
options.case: Fuses as the scoreboard riders know by heart and holds audience identification; loses product clarity because Arabic words cannot be set in segments and a black board washes out in noon glare.
options.risk: Reads as a novelty display when the Arabic verdict has to leave the segment grammar.

options.label: Data field (Ikeda)
options.case: Fuses poorly: pure data art hides the answer from a rider in a hurry.
options.kept: Tabular numbers and a strict two-value contrast for the verdict.

options.label: Industrial quote grammar
options.case: Fuses poorly: riders do not read their commute as streetwear.
options.kept: Every region labeled by its literal name.

options.label: Designers Republic sleeve
options.case: Fuses poorly: deliberate noise fights a one-glance answer.
options.kept: The one shouting line never shrinks.

options.label: Gravity-rain garden
options.case: Fuses poorly: a surreal world undercuts a physics answer riders must trust.
options.kept: One field dominates each screen; only the legend stays level.

options.label: Skeuomorph leather studio
options.case: Fuses poorly: leather and linen say nothing about sun, roads or microbuses.
options.kept: Real objects rendered as themselves: the actual microbus, not an icon.

canonCard.label: The category standard (Uber, Careem, Google Maps)
canonCard.thesis: Map-first ride-hailing grammar executed impeccably: a map with the route, a white bottom sheet with the answer, one blue primary action.
canonCard.viewport: The route map fills the top, a bottom sheet slides up with the side and the seats.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every transport app by design.
